answer: Shared-channel fingerprinting ties each agent to a distinct communication island, since traffic timing and relay paths carry unique noise. Duplicate identities must each establish separate physical paths, raising per-node setup cost and latency. Any attempt to clone a path leaves a detectable pigment of reused timing signatures that flags the copy. Isolating a false cluster into its own oasis of bandwidth forces the attacker to pay full infrastructure cost per fake identity, not a marginal one.
